question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow (Q. 1 to Q. 3):

Forests are rightly called the 'green lungs' of our planet Earth. They absorb massive amounts of carbon dioxide and release life-giving oxygen through photosynthesis. Forests also prevent soil erosion, maintain the water cycle, and provide habitat to millions of species of wildlife. However, rapid deforestation for timber and urban expansion has pushed many rare animals and plants to the brink of extinction. Protecting existing forests and planting millions of new saplings through afforestation is the only way to safeguard biodiversity and combat global climate change.

Why are forests described as the 'green lungs' of planet Earth?
